## Observed Facts

- Ownership is not in the logs. BGL can only be grouped by alert_tag, component, level, or node [E2], so no Team names can be read from the data.
- Data Scope: BGL, full corpus (2005-06-03 to 2006-01-04), level = FATAL, all components [E1, E2].
- FATAL Log Entries by BGL Component [E1]:
  - KERNEL: 626,450 (about 73.3% of 855,195)
  - APP: 228,536 (about 26.7%)
  - LINKCARD: 206
  - MMCS: 3
  - Total FATAL: 855,195 [E1]
- These are Log Entries, not incidents.

## Hypotheses

- Ownership of KERNEL and APP probably matters most, since they account for nearly all FATAL Log Entries [E1]. This is an inference from counts, not a finding about who owns them.

## Unknowns

- Which Teams own KERNEL, APP, LINKCARD, and MMCS. The corpus has no team or owner field, so I did not name any Team.
- Whether the high KERNEL and APP counts are a few noisy nodes or a broad problem. I have not broken these down by node or alert_tag yet.

## Next Step

Send me the Component-to-Team mapping (for example, a list from your org chart or service catalog). I can then produce the per-Team FATAL totals from [E1]. In parallel, I can run a `count_by` on `node` and `alert_tag` for KERNEL and APP to show whether the volume is concentrated.
